question: What directional relationship do yellow center line markings and white lane line markings communicate?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Color communicates direction of travel: yellow markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions, while white markings separate traffic moving in the same direction. Thus a driver seeing a yellow line on the left knows opposing traffic is on the other side, whereas white lane lines indicate the adjacent lane travels the same way. Reversible lanes use broken double yellow lines because they serve as the center line at some times. Standards (mandatory): - "Center line pavement markings, when used, shall be the pavement markings used to delineate the separation of traffic lanes that have opposite directions of travel on a roadway and shall be yellow." - "When used, lane line pavement markings delineating the separation of traffic lanes that have the same direction of travel shall be white." - On two-lane, two-way roadways, center line markings shall be one of: "Two-direction passing zone markings consisting of a normal width broken yellow line…"; "One-direction no-passing zone markings consisting of a double yellow line, one of which is a normal width broken yellow line and the other is a normal width solid yellow line…"; or "Two-direction no-passing zone markings consisting of two normal width solid yellow lines…" - "Except where a reversible lane (see Section 3B.04) or a two-way left-turn lane (see Section 3B.05) is present, the center line markings on undivided two-way roadways with four or more lanes for moving motor vehicle traffic always available shall be the two-direction no-passing zone markings consisting of normal width double solid yellow lines as shown in Figure 3B-2." - "If reversible lanes are used, the lane line pavement markings on each side of reversible lanes shall consist of a normal width broken double yellow line to delineate the edge of a lane in which the direction of travel is reversed from time to time, such that each of these markings serve as the center line markings of the roadway during some period (see Figure 3B-6)." - "A normal width dotted white line marking shall be used as the lane line to separate a through lane that continues beyond the interchange or intersection from an adjacent deceleration or acceleration lane." Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 3B-2 shows multi-lane, two-way roadways where double solid yellow lines separate the opposing directions (arrows pointing opposite ways) while broken white lane lines separate lanes traveling in the same direction. - [Image 2] Figure 3B-3 shows three-lane, two-way applications in which the yellow center line (broken-plus-solid or double solid) divides opposing flows and the white lane line separates the two same-direction lanes. - [Image 3] Figure 3B-1 shows two-lane, two-way applications with broken and solid yellow center lines between opposing arrows, illustrating passing and no-passing zone messages. - [Image 4] Page 582 repeats Figure 3B-3, showing the yellow center line between opposite-direction arrows and the white line between same-direction arrows. - [Image 5] Page 583 repeats Figure 3B-2, with the double yellow center line dividing opposing traffic and white lines dividing same-direction lanes, including left-turn channelization outlined in yellow. - [Image 6] Page 595 (Figure 3B-11, lane-drop markings) shows all-white lane and channelizing lines between same-direction freeway lanes, with yellow only along the left edge of the directional roadway. - [Image 7] Page 674 (Figure 3I-1) shows a two-way street where the yellow center line separates opposing arrows and white lane lines separate same-direction lanes near a crosswalk. Citations: - Section 3B.01 Standard §1 (p.540) - Section 3B.01 Standard §4 (p.540) - Section 3B.01 Standard §6 (p.540) - Section 3B.06 Standard §1 (p.546) - Section 3B.07 Standard §1 (p.548) - Section 3B.04 Standard §1 (p.543) - Figure 3B-2 (p.541) - Figure 3B-3 (p.542) - Figure 3B-1 (p.540) - Page 582 - Page 583 - Page 595 - Page 674
gold_answer: Yellow center lines separate lanes traveling in opposite directions. White lane lines separate lanes traveling in the same direction.
